title: Federated convex bandits: synchronous two-point feedback and periodic communication
summary: Multiple clients face local convex Lipschitz losses and communicate only at specified synchronization rounds. Each client simultaneously queries two values of its current local function, and both points incur loss. The comparator is one fixed point shared by all clients.

task.formulation: Multiple clients face local convex Lipschitz losses and communicate only at specified synchronization rounds. Each client simultaneously queries two values of its current local function, and both points incur loss. The comparator is one fixed point shared by all clients.
task.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.
description_paragraphs: Multiple clients face local convex Lipschitz losses and communicate only at specified synchronization rounds. Each client simultaneously queries two values of its current local function, and both points incur loss. The comparator is one fixed point shared by all clients.

model.instance: There are $M$ clients interacting simultaneously in $\mathbb R^d$ for $T=L_{\mathrm{comm}}R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds each. They synchronize once every $L_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds, for $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ synchronizations. Each $f_t^m:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and convex, with uniform Euclidean Lipschitz constant $G$ on the whole space. $$f_t(x)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x),\qquad \frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\|\nabla f_t^m(x)-\nabla f_t(x)\|_2^2\le\zeta^2\quad(\forall t,x).$$ The adversary may depend on all past actions and the algorithm, but not on its current private randomness. All clients share the same hindsight comparator: $$x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\|x\|_2\le B}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x).$$

operations.query_signature: Each client simultaneously submits $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ and receives exact values of the same current local function at both points. The second point cannot depend on the first response. There is no independent measurement noise; variance from randomized directions is part of the estimator analysis. Both query points incur loss. The comparator ball $\{x:\|x\|_2\le B\}$ does not restrict all queries. Inputs $M,d,T,L_{\mathrm{comm}},R_{\mathrm{comm}},G,B,\zeta$ are public. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.
